units.title: Theme A: Living together in the UK

outcomes.text: Describe how the UK population's age, ethnicity, religion and disability mix is changing.
Explain the social, economic and other effects of immigration, as benefit and challenge.
Tell apart economic migrants, refugees and asylum seekers and why people migrate.
Describe sources of migration to the UK since 1945, including the Commonwealth and Europe.
Explain mutual respect, and the effects of inequality and discrimination, and the Equality Act 2010.
Explain how schools and communities encourage understanding, diversity, integration and community cohesion.
Explain the different ways identity is defined and multiple identities.
Explain how the UK's four nations affect identity debates.

topics.title: 5 Rights, duties and values that underpin democracy

outcomes.text: Describe human, moral, legal and political rights and freedoms in the UK.
Explain citizens' duties to respect others' rights and obey the law.
Explain how rights can conflict and need balancing.
Explain why the rule of law matters and the debates over speech, privacy and terrorism.
Explain Magna Carta as a first step against arbitrary rule.
Describe rights protected by the UN Declaration, European Convention, Convention on the Rights of the Child and Human Rights Act 1998.
Tell councillors from officers and describe what councils do.
Explain how councils are funded: council tax, business rates, grants and charges.

units.title: Theme B: Democracy at work in the UK

outcomes.text: Explain key philosophical differences between the major parties.
Describe how candidates are selected for a constituency.
Compare representative and direct democracy, including strengths and weaknesses.
Explain how first-past-the-post works, who can vote, debates on the franchise and election frequency.
Compare first-past-the-post with proportional representation.

topics.title: 3 Forming and organising the work of government

outcomes.text: Explain forming a government, the monarch's role and coalitions.
Describe government departments, ministries and agencies staffed by civil servants.
Distinguish executive, legislature, judiciary and monarchy.
Explain the Commons, Lords and parliamentary debate in shaping policy and legislation.
Describe the roles of prime minister, cabinet, opposition, speaker, whips, MPs and Black Rod.
Explain how a bill becomes law: both Houses, committee scrutiny and royal assent.
Describe the institutions of the British constitution and their roles.
Explain the uncodified constitution and how devolution and EU membership changed it.
Explain parliamentary sovereignty, judicial review and how Parliament holds government to account.

topics.title: 7 Government in constituent parts of the UK

outcomes.text: Describe the powers of devolved bodies in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
Explain changing relations between the four nations, devolution and independence.
Explain how direct and indirect taxes are raised.
Describe the Chancellor's role in budgeting and allocating funding.
Discuss debates over welfare, health, elderly care and education provision.

topics.title: 1 The role of law in everyday life

outcomes.text: Explain what law is and how it affects everyday life.
Explain why we need laws: protection, disputes, fairness, justice, changing behaviour and new situations.
Explain legal ages of responsibility and criminal responsibility, and why age limits protect young people.
Explain the rule of law, presumption of innocence, equality before the law and access to justice.
Explain how England and Wales differ legally from Northern Ireland and Scotland.
Tell common law from legislation as sources of law.
Explain the purposes of criminal law.
Explain the purposes of civil law, such as debt, injury and family disputes.

topics.title: 4 The justice system in England and Wales

outcomes.text: Describe the roles and powers of police, judges, magistrates and legal representatives.
Describe citizens' roles as jurors, magistrates, special constables and tribunal members.
Explain the rights of arrested citizens.
Compare magistrates and crown courts and the cases they hear.
Describe county and high courts.
Explain tribunals and mediation as ways to settle disputes.
Explain how the youth justice system works and why youth courts differ.
Explain factors affecting crime rates, recording of crime and re-offending.
Describe strategies to reduce crime: prevention, protection and punishment.
Describe sentences such as prison, community payback and restorative justice and how they are decided.
Discuss the purposes and impact of different punishments.

topics.title: 1 Citizen participation in politics and society

outcomes.text: Explain opportunities and barriers to participation in UK democracy.
Describe direct and indirect ways citizens act: voting, parties, standing, campaigning, lobbying, petitions, demonstrations, volunteering.
Explain how digital democracy and social media may improve engagement.
Compare participation in one democratic and one non-democratic system outside the UK.

topics.title: 2 The role of groups and organisations in democratic society

outcomes.text: Describe how public bodies, interest and pressure groups, trade unions, charities and voluntary groups give people a voice.
Give two examples of citizens working together to change their communities.
Explain the role and origins of trade unions.
Describe workplace rights and the protection from unions, staff associations and tribunals.

topics.title: 3 The role of the media and a free press

outcomes.text: Explain why a free press matters: informing, accurate news, investigating, and holding power to account.

topics.title: 4 Rights and responsibilities of the media

outcomes.text: Explain media rights to investigate subject to accuracy, privacy and dignity.
Explain the press regulator and why censorship may occur.

topics.title: 5 The use of the media for influence

outcomes.text: Explain how groups, individuals and those in power use the media to influence opinion.

topics.title: 6 The UK's role and relations with Europe

outcomes.text: Tell apart the European Union and the Council of Europe.
Explain how UK-EU relations changed after Brexit on migration, fishing, travel and trade.

topics.title: 7 The UK's role in the rest of the world

outcomes.text: Describe the UN, NATO, Commonwealth and WTO and the UK's benefits and commitments as a member.

topics.title: 8 Rights and responsibilities in challenging global situations

outcomes.text: Explain balancing rights and responsibilities in global conflicts.
Explain how international humanitarian law limits the effects of war on civilians.
Describe how NGOs give relief and support development.
Give an example of the UK's role in an international dispute using mediation, sanctions or force.
Identify a citizenship issue, form a team of two or more and carry out secondary research.
Understand methods governments, groups and individuals use to address issues.
Write and sequence research questions and carry out primary research.
Analyse answers to decide the activity.
Show understanding of the issue and different views, and judge which evidence is more persuasive.
Make the case for what should happen.
Set target audience, goals and success criteria.
Plan steps, sequence and priorities with roles, difficulties and a record of progress.
Show teamwork, negotiation and influence.
Deliver an advocacy event or campaign, or a social action project or community action.
Evaluate how and why the action met its goals and how well the method worked.
Reflect on the impact on your own citizenship learning.
